questions.question: The Human Development Index was launched in the first Human Development Report (1990) by:
options: Mahbub ul Haq working with Amartya Sen
The World Bank under Robert McNamara
questions.rationale: Mahbub ul Haq conceived the HDR/HDI in partnership with Amartya Sen, whose capabilities approach underpins it; the 1990 report opens with 'People are the real wealth of a nation'.

questions.question: Which three dimensions does the HDI measure?
options: A long and healthy life, knowledge, a decent standard of living
questions.rationale: HDI combines life expectancy at birth (health), expected and mean years of schooling (knowledge), and GNI per capita in PPP dollars (living standard).

questions.question: In the HDI, GNI per capita enters through:
options: A logarithm over goalposts of US$100 to 75,000
Purchasing-power parity of the median wage
questions.rationale: Income uses a logarithm between $100 and $75,000 so each extra dollar counts less as income rises — richer people's dollars matter less to the index.

questions.question: An HDI value of 0.644 would place a country in which development band?
questions.rationale: The bands are: below 0.550 low; 0.550-0.699 medium; 0.700-0.799 high; 0.800+ very high. India's roughly 0.64 sits in the medium band.

questions.question: The inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) matters because:
options: National averages can hide deep distributional gaps in health, schooling, and income
It adds GDP growth to the HDI
It replaces GNI with median income
questions.rationale: HDI averages can mask inequality; the IHDI discounts each dimension for its distributional spread, and India's loss from inequality is roughly a fifth of its HDI.

questions.question: The Multidimensional Poverty Index declares a household poor when it is deprived in:
options: At least income and education only
A weighted one-third of the ten indicators
questions.rationale: MPI poverty begins when weighted deprivations cross one-third across the ten indicators of health, education, and living standards — income itself is not counted.

questions.question: UNDP estimates about how many Indians exited multidimensional poverty between 2005-06 and 2019-21?
questions.rationale: UNDP-OPHI estimate roughly 415 million people moved out of multidimensional poverty in 15 years — the global MPI headcount fell from 55.1% to 16.4%.

questions.question: 'Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs' comes from:
options: The Brundtland Report, Our Common Future, 1987
questions.rationale: This is the canonical Brundtland definition of sustainable development, stressing intergenerational equity; Stockholm (1972) was the first UN environment conference.

questions.question: The Sustainable Development Goals adopted in 2015 consist of:
options: 8 goals and 21 targets for developing countries
17 goals and 169 targets, universal for all countries
17 goals binding only on the G20
questions.rationale: The 2030 Agenda has 17 goals and 169 targets effective from 1 January 2016, and unlike the MDGs they are universal — applying to rich and poor countries alike.

questions.question: Under its updated Nationally Determined Contributions and the COP26 pledge, India has committed to:
options: 45% cut in emissions intensity and 50% non-fossil power capacity by 2030, with net zero by 2070
A 2.5-3 billion tonne increase in oil reserves
questions.rationale: India's NDCs target a 45% reduction in GDP emissions intensity and about 50% non-fossil installed capacity by 2030, plus a forest carbon sink of 2.5-3 bn tonnes; the net-zero year is 2070.
